identificationModule.briefTitle: Effectiveness of Nutritional Products to Treat Moderate Acute Malnutrition
identificationModule.officialTitle: Using Indigenous Foods to Reduce Malnutrition in Children

leadSponsor.name: Centre for Food and Nutrition Research, Yaounde

descriptionModule.briefSummary: The purpose of this study is to determine whether an improved corn-soya blend (CSB+) and a new formulated ready-to-use supplementary food (RUSF) are effective in the treatment of moderate acute malnutrition in children.
descriptionModule.detailedDescription: Assuming the availability of some food in the household, the caregivers were instructed on how best to use the food they have and the quantity of supplementary food distributed was calculated to provide about 50% of child energy requirement.

armGroups.label: Ready to Use Suplementary Food (RUSF)
armGroups.description: A daily ration of 40 kcal/kg of body weight during 56 days
interventionNames: Dietary Supplement: A daily ration of 40 kcal/kg of body weight during 56 days

armGroups.label: Corn Soya Blend (CSB+)
armGroups.description: A daily ration of 40 kcal/kg of body weight during 56 days
interventionNames: Dietary Supplement: A daily ration of 40 kcal/kg of body weight during 56 days

interventions.name: A daily ration of 40 kcal/kg of body weight during 56 days
interventions.description: On enrollment, children were examined by a pediatrician to assess their health status and they were de-wormed with one tablet of Mebendazole 500 mg.

primaryOutcomes.measure: Recovery rate of the children receiving CSB+ or RUSF

eligibilityModule.eligibilityCriteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Children aged 6-59 month
* Weight-for-height between -3 and -2 z-scores without edema
* Good appetite
* Stable clinical conditions

Exclusion Criteria:

* Weight-for-Height Z-score \< -3
* Presence of bilateral pitting edema
* Unstable clinical conditions
* Not showing appetite
